method.title: The method
method.lede: Our books are not books you write in a little. They are built on two memory mechanisms documented for decades. Here they are — and how far they go.
recit: You have read a text through, closed the book, and found you could not say three sentences about it. That is not a lapse of attention. It is what reading alone does: it gives the feeling of knowing, which is not knowing.
Writing breaks that illusion. It forces you to choose a word, and so to decide; to phrase a thought, and so to understand it. What costs effort leaves a trace — and no screen asks that effort of you.
Our books are built on this. You read a real text, then you must return to it to answer, then you write something that belongs to you alone. Three stages, in that order, each for a precise reason.

affirmations.phrase: What you produce, you remember. What you read, you merely recognise.
affirmations.source: Slamecka & Graf, 1978 — the generation effect, established across five experiments.

affirmations.phrase: Testing yourself beats rereading. For the same time spent.
affirmations.source: Roediger & Karpicke, 2006 — the testing effect, one of the most robust findings in the psychology of learning.

affirmations.phrase: Our books do not engage one mechanism. They engage two.
affirmations.source: The generation effect and the testing effect are distinct phenomena. Writing your answer, then having to retrieve it, is not the same work.

affirmations.phrase: On screen, comprehension drops. And the gap has widened over the years.
affirmations.source: Delgado, Vargas, Ackerman & Salmerón, 2018 — a meta-analysis of 54 studies and over 170,000 participants. The paper advantage grows across the period analysed: this is not a generational matter, and digital natives are no exception.
affirmations.limite: The gap concerns expository texts, the ones read in order to learn. For narrative texts, another meta-analysis finds no difference. We do not claim paper always wins.

affirmations.phrase: Nearly half a million readers: digital leisure reading barely improves comprehension.
affirmations.source: Altamura, Vargas & Salmerón, Review of Educational Research — 469,564 participants. The effect is close to nil, where print reading habits show medium effects. Among younger readers the relationship is even negative.
affirmations.limite: This is a correlation, not proof of cause. Reading a great deal on screen does not mechanically damage comprehension: it simply does not build it, as print does.

affirmations.phrase: Writing by hand engages the brain more widely than typing.
affirmations.source: Van der Weel & Van der Meer, 2024 — high-density EEG, 256 sensors.
affirmations.limite: This study measures brain connectivity, not learning outcomes. It received a published critical commentary in the same journal. We cite it for what it shows, not for what we would like it to say.

affirmations.phrase: Writing what you feel has been studied for forty years. The effect is real. It is small.
affirmations.source: The expressive writing paradigm, opened by Pennebaker. An early meta-analysis (Smyth, 1998) found a medium effect; across the hundred-plus studies accumulated since, the average falls to around d = 0.16.
affirmations.limite: The results replicate poorly, and it remains unclear which conditions are required to obtain them. The writer's actual engagement appears to explain part of the variation. We say so because it is true, not in spite of it.

affirmations.phrase: The gratitude journal has been tested in controlled trials. 25 trials, 6,745 participants, effect g = 0.22.
affirmations.source: A meta-analysis of randomised trials on psychological wellbeing — life satisfaction, positive affect, happiness. The practice goes back to Emmons and McCullough (2003).
affirmations.limite: 0.22 is a small effect. The literature presents it as a complement, never as a treatment. A journal does not cure depression.

affirmations.phrase: We publish the effect sizes. That is why we are able to cite them.
affirmations.source: A small measured effect is worth more than a spectacular unverifiable one. Those who write « scientifically proven » without ever giving a figure are counting on nobody checking.

affirmations.phrase: The most-cited study on handwriting was never replicated.
affirmations.source: Mueller & Oppenheimer, 2014 — the one that had laptops banned from entire lecture halls. In 2019, Morehead, Dunlosky and Rawson ran the protocol again: a small effect, and not significant.
affirmations.limite: We do not use it. It is nonetheless the one that would be cited in our place.

affirmations.phrase: A book is not a therapy.
affirmations.source: Our books for older readers draw on life-review practices, which are studied. They do not replace them.
affirmations.limite: We promise no preserved memory, no slowed decline, no medical benefit. Anyone promising you that is lying.

method.regle: Every claim carries its source. And its limit.
method.regleSuite: A competitor can copy a book. They will not copy that discipline, because it costs work: you have to read the studies, including the ones that contradict you.

legalNotice.title: Legal notice
legalNotice.lede: Who publishes this site, who is responsible for it, and where it is hosted.

sections.heading: Purpose of this site
sections.body: This site presents the publishing house's catalogue and its news. It sells nothing directly: each book is offered for purchase on Amazon, where the order, payment, delivery and after-sales service are governed by Amazon and its own terms.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
sections.body: The texts, images, covers and graphic elements shown on this site are protected. Published works remain the property of their authors, within the limits of the rights assigned to the publishing house. Any reproduction or representation, in whole or in part, without prior written permission is prohibited.

sections.heading: Links to third-party sites
sections.body: This site links to Amazon pages. Those pages are not published by the publishing house, which has no control over their content or over the terms that apply to them.

sections.heading: Reporting content
sections.body: Any request concerning content published on this site may be sent to the contact address above. It will be handled as promptly as possible.

termsOfSale.title: Terms of sale
termsOfSale.lede: This site does not sell directly. Here is what that means for you.

sections.heading: No sale is concluded on this site
sections.body: This site is a showcase. It offers no basket, no payment and no customer account. Your visit therefore creates no contract of sale between you and the publishing house.

sections.heading: The sale is concluded by Amazon
sections.body: Every purchase button takes you to Amazon. There, the order, payment, invoicing, delivery, right of withdrawal and after-sales service are governed by Amazon's terms, Amazon being your seller. The publishing house takes part in none of these steps.

sections.heading: The price shown
sections.body: The price shown on this site is the public price set by the publisher. In France, the law of 10 August 1981 reserves the setting of a book's price to its publisher and caps at 5% the discount a retailer may grant. The price seen at a retailer may therefore differ slightly, within that limit.

sections.heading: If direct sale is ever opened
sections.body: On the day a purchase can be completed on this site, full terms of sale will be published here before it goes live, and shown to you before any payment.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy
privacyPolicy.lede: What this site collects, why, for how long, and how to take back control.

sections.heading: The principle
sections.body: This site collects the bare minimum. The only personal data collected is the email address you choose to leave in order to hear about new releases. No other information is requested.

sections.heading: Signing up for release announcements
sections.body: The form collects your email address and your explicit consent, through a box that is never pre-ticked. You may also indicate which book you are waiting for. No other information is requested, and no field is inferred or filled in without your knowledge.

sections.heading: Double opt-in
sections.body: Your sign-up is not recorded straight away. You receive an email containing a link valid for forty-eight hours: until you follow it, your address is added to no list. That link is cryptographically signed and carries the information itself, so nothing is stored on our servers between your request and your confirmation.

sections.heading: What this processing rests on
sections.body: Your consent, freely given, which you may withdraw at any time, without having to justify yourself and with no consequence.

sections.heading: Who receives your data
sections.body: Your address is entrusted to the provider that delivers our emails, {fournisseur}, acting as a processor and for that sole purpose. It is neither sold, nor rented, nor passed on to anyone else.

sections.heading: How long it is kept
sections.body: Your address is kept for as long as you remain subscribed, then erased within three years of your last contact with us, in line with the French data protection authority's recommendation on marketing.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability. You may unsubscribe at any time using the link in every email, or write to the contact address above. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.body: One cookie is used: it remembers which Amazon store you choose on a book page, so that you are not asked again on every visit. It contains only a country code, no identifier, and serves only the service you asked for yourself. You may delete it from your browser at any time.

sections.heading: What happens when you buy
sections.body: Purchases are completed on Amazon. The moment you leave this site, Amazon's privacy policy and terms apply, and we receive no information about your order.

shippingReturns.title: Shipping and returns
shippingReturns.lede: They do not depend on this site.

sections.heading: Who ships the books
sections.body: This site ships nothing. Orders placed through the purchase buttons are handled by Amazon, which takes care of preparation, shipping and tracking.

sections.heading: Times and shipping costs
sections.body: The stated times, shipping costs and delivery methods are Amazon's. They are shown on the book's page at the time of ordering.

sections.heading: Returns, exchanges and refunds
sections.body: These are handled by Amazon, under its terms, including the exercise of the right of withdrawal. The publishing house has access neither to your order nor to your file.

sections.heading: A damaged or incorrect book
sections.body: Report it first to Amazon, which is your seller and the only party able to act on your order. You may also write to us: it does not replace that step, but we want to know.
